newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy drugs trial of British teenager suspended.
newsitem.headline: Italy drugs trial of British teenager suspended.

text.p: An Italian juvenile court suspended the heroin smuggling trial of a 17-year-old British girl on Wednesday and ordered a period of probation instead.

Marianne Platt of Croydon, south London, was arrested near Naples last June with another British teenager after police discovered four kg (nine lbs) of heroin in a hidden compartment of a holdall they were carrying.
The drug's street value was estimated at $600,000.
The girls had arrived at Rome's Fiumicino airport on a flight from Istanbul, police said.
"If the probation period goes well, at the end of it she will be able to put it all behind her," Platt's Italian lawyer, Susanna Spaford, told Reuters.
Spaford said the judge indicated that the case would be shelved if Platt lived up to all the terms of the probation, which would be announced at a hearing on February 5.
The lawyer said the probation would have to be served in Italy and probably would involve a work-study programme.
"I think the judge realised that Marianne was somehow dragged into this and was not completely aware of what was going on," the lawyer said in a telephone interview.
"Marianne accepted the idea (of probation) because this way she will have no consequences in her future life. She can have a completely normal life after this is over," Spaford said.

Platt has been living in a special home for youths in Rome run by state social services and will remain there for the time being, Spaford said. Platt, wearing a black jacket and trousers and with her blonde hair pulled back in a ponytail, attended Wednesday's hearing with her mother but made no comment.

The case against the other British girl, 19-year-old Melanie Jackman of Brighton, southern England, was being heard separately because she is not a minor. She has been remanded in a jail near Naples since the arrest.

Both girls have said they did not know they were carrying drugs. Jackman's parents have been quoted as saying Melanie told them she thought she was bringing money to Italy for a man she had befriended on Brighton pier last April.
